notes.md: - **Article 370 judgment (11 Dec 2023):** a **five-judge** Constitution Bench headed by CJI **D.Y. Chandrachud** upheld the abrogation **unanimously**; it directed J&K Assembly elections by **30 September 2024** and restoration of statehood at the earliest.

new.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Waman Rao case
2. First Amendment creating the Ninth Schedule
3. I.R. Coelho case
4. Kesavananda Bharati case
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: First Amendment (1951), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), Waman Rao (1981), I.R. Coelho (2007).
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: Ninth Schedule sequence 1951-1973-1981-2007

new.s: In which year did the Supreme Court decide the I.R. Coelho case on Ninth Schedule laws?
new.x: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) held that Ninth Schedule laws have no blanket immunity.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: I.R. Coelho -> year

new.s: In which case was harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles held to be a basic feature of the Constitution?
new.x: Minerva Mills (1980) held judicial review, limited amending power and FR-DPSP harmony to be basic features.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: Minerva Mills -> FR-DPSP harmony

new.s: Which of the following was NOT held to be a basic feature in Minerva Mills (1980)?
o: Harmony between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
Powers of the High Courts under Articles 226 and 227
new.x: The basic-structure status of High Court powers under Articles 226 and 227 came in L. Chandra Kumar (1997), not Minerva Mills.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: Minerva Mills -> elements (NOT)

new.s: In which case was the independence of the judiciary upheld as a basic feature while striking down the 99th Amendment?
new.x: The NJAC case (2015) struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act, holding judicial independence basic.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: NJAC -> independent judiciary

new.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold, by a nine-judge bench, that secularism and federalism are basic features and misuse of Article 356 is open to review?
new.x: S.R. Bommai (1994), a nine-judge bench, dealt with Article 356 misuse and held secularism and federalism basic.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: S.R. Bommai -> Art. 356, nine judges

new.s: Which Constitutional Amendment was upheld by the Supreme Court in Sajjan Singh (1965)?
new.x: Sajjan Singh (1965) upheld the 17th Amendment and reaffirmed Shankari Prasad.
new.angle: U0295 notes gap: Sajjan Singh -> 17th Amendment upheld

new.s: Which judgment of the Supreme Court laid down that the majority of a government must be tested on the floor of the House?
new.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) made Article 356 reviewable and held that majority must be tested by a floor test.
new.angle: U0296 notes gap: floor test -> S.R. Bommai

new.s: Who was the Chief Justice of India when the Shayara Bano, Navtej Johar and Aadhaar judgments were delivered?
new.x: The notes link Shayara Bano, Navtej Johar and Aadhaar to CJI Dipak Misra; Puttaswamy to Khehar.
new.angle: U0296 #8 case -> chief justice (Dipak Misra)

new.s: In which year did the Andhra Pradesh High Court rule against the three-capitals plan?
new.x: The AP High Court ruled against three capitals in 2022; Amaravati became the sole capital from 2 June 2024.
new.angle: U0296 #9 AP capital case -> year

new.s: How many judges were on the Constitution Bench that upheld the abrogation of Article 370 in December 2023?
new.x: A five-judge Constitution Bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud unanimously upheld the abrogation on 11 December 2023.
new.angle: U0296 #13 Article 370 judgment -> bench strength (web)

new.s: By what date did the Supreme Court direct elections to the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly in its Article 370 judgment?
new.x: The December 2023 judgment directed the Election Commission to hold J&K Assembly elections by 30 September 2024.
new.angle: U0296 #13 Article 370 judgment -> directions (web)

new.s: From which country does the doctrine of pleasure come?
new.x: The doctrine of pleasure (Art. 310) comes from England.
new.angle: U0297 notes gap: pleasure -> England

new.s: Which case is associated with the doctrine of severability?
new.x: Under severability only the invalid part of a law goes; the notes link it to R.M.D.C. (1957).
new.angle: U0297 notes gap: severability -> R.M.D.C.

new.s: On which country's constitution did Montesquieu mainly draw for his theory of separation of powers?
new.x: Montesquieu's 'The Spirit of Laws' (1748) drew on the British constitution.
new.angle: U0298 notes gap: Montesquieu -> British constitution

new.s: Who was the first woman President of India?
new.x: Pratibha Patil (2007-12) was the first woman President.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: first woman President

new.s: Who is the first tribal President of India?
new.x: Droupadi Murmu, President from 25 July 2022, is the first tribal President.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: first tribal President

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (President)
a. S. Radhakrishnan
b. K.R. Narayanan
c. Pratibha Patil
d. Droupadi Murmu
List-II (First)
1. First woman President
2. First tribal President
3. First President from South India
4. First Dalit President
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: Radhakrishnan was the first from South India, Narayanan the first Dalit, Patil the first woman and Murmu the first tribal President.
new.angle: U0299 #9 Presidents -> firsts (match)

new.s: In which year was the honorific 'His Excellency' for the President of India dropped?
new.x: President Pranab Mukherjee dropped 'His Excellency' in 2012.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: 'His Excellency' dropped 2012

new.s: How many proposers and seconders does a candidate for the office of President need at present?
new.x: Since 1997 a Presidential nomination needs 50 proposers and 50 seconders; earlier it was 10 and 10.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: nomination 50 + 50

new.s: The President addresses his resignation to the Vice-President. To whom does the Vice-President communicate it?
new.x: The resignation goes to the Vice-President, who informs the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: resignation -> VP informs Speaker

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President addresses his resignation to the Chief Justice of India.
2. The Vice-President informs the Speaker of the Lok Sabha of the President's resignation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The resignation is addressed to the Vice-President (not the CJI), who informs the Speaker.
new.angle: U0299 #3 resignation addressed to whom (statements)

new.s: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces of India?
new.x: The President is the Supreme Commander; he declares war and makes peace on the Council's advice.
new.angle: U0299 #5 military power -> Supreme Commander

new.s: For which of the following Bills, besides Money Bills, is the prior recommendation of the President required?
o: Bills under Article 3 on forming new States or altering State boundaries
new.x: Money Bills and Article 3 Bills (new States, boundaries) need the President's prior recommendation.
new.angle: U0299 notes gap: prior recommendation -> Art. 3 Bills

new.s: On which occasions does the President address both Houses of Parliament together?
o: First session after each general election and first session of each year
new.x: Under Article 87 the President addresses the first session after each general election and the first session of each year.
new.angle: U0299 #15 legislative powers -> special address

new.s:
Consider the following statements about an ordinance issued by the President:
1. It ceases to operate six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved.
2. It ceases earlier if both Houses pass resolutions disapproving it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: An ordinance lapses six weeks after reassembly, and ends earlier if both Houses disapprove it or it is withdrawn.
new.angle: U0300 notes gap: ordinance ends on disapproval of both Houses

new.s: In which of the following cases does an ordinance end before six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament?
o: When the Supreme Court is in vacation
When both Houses pass resolutions disapproving it
When the Lok Sabha Speaker objects
new.x: Disapproval by resolutions of both Houses, or withdrawal by the President, ends an ordinance earlier.
new.angle: U0300 #2 ordinance -> end by disapproval

new.s: Under which Article did Andhra Pradesh use an ordinance on organ-transplant committees?
new.x: The Governor's ordinance power is Article 213; AP used it for organ-transplant committees.
new.angle: U0300 notes gap: AP ordinance -> Art. 213
